workExperienceSection.workDescription:
• Own the fraud model that scores 40 million card transactions a day, raising recall at the same false-positive rate by 9 points
• Built a feature store on Spark and Redis that serves 300 features in under 10 ms, shared by four product teams
• Moved model training from Jupyter notebooks to scheduled pipelines with automatic evaluation and rollback, so a retrained model ships in one day instead of after two weeks of manual checks
• Set up shadow deployments that score live traffic with a candidate model for a week before it replaces the old one
• Mentor two junior engineers and lead the team's monthly reading group on fraud and anomaly detection papers

• Trained a transformer on sequences of login events to spot account takeovers, finding 30% more attacks than the rule-based system at the same alert volume for the security operations team
• Distilled the model to a quarter of its size so it runs on the existing CPU fleet without buying any new hardware

• Studied how fraud labels that arrive weeks late skew model calibration, and built a correction method that is now part of the lab's open-source toolkit and used in two follow-up papers by other students in the lab
• Ran experiments on 200 million public transactions using the university's GPU cluster and shared all the code

projectsSection.projectDescription: • A from-scratch autograd engine with a written guide to backpropagation, used as course reading in two university classes

• Graph neural network that forecasts traffic speed on major Lagos roads an hour ahead from public GPS data
• Served the forecasts through a FastAPI endpoint that a local ride-hailing startup tested for routing drivers
